choices: No — 'beats more often' need not be transitive; non-transitive dice exist where C actually beats A
Only if all three dice have six sides

questions.q: Drug A has a higher overall cure rate than Drug B when you pool all patients together. Must Drug A also have a higher cure rate than Drug B within every age subgroup considered separately?
choices: Only if both drugs have a cure rate above 50%
Yes, this is guaranteed by the laws of probability
No — this relationship can reverse within subgroups (Simpson's Paradox)
Only if the two drugs were tested on equal numbers of patients

questions.q: A rare side effect occurs independently in 1% of patients who take a certain drug. If 100 patients take the drug, is it certain (100%) that at least one will experience the side effect? What is the actual probability, rounded to the nearest percent?
choices: Yes, 100% — a 1% chance times 100 patients guarantees at least one
No, it is not certain — the actual probability is about 63%

You will interview candidates one at a time in random order for a single position, and must accept or permanently reject each one immediately, with the goal of maximizing your chance of hiring the single best candidate overall. The optimal strategy is to automatically reject the first k candidates (using them only to set a benchmark), then hire the next one who is better than everyone seen so far. As the candidate pool grows large, what fraction of candidates should you plan to automatically reject before switching to the hire-if-best-so-far rule?

choices: She used a time machine to undo it.
She is a ghost and none of it really happened.
She develops a photograph of him — 'shoots' with a camera, 'holds' the film underwater to develop it, and 'hangs' it up to dry.
It's all a dream she is having.
